El peleador del Climent Club, consolidado con un interesante 3-0 en su carrera como profesional, peleará este fin de semana en WOW 33 Vitoria contra el durísimo Willmar Quirama (4-0-1) en una prueba de nivel para saber a qué puede aspirar Richardson. En la previa de este combate, atiende a MARCA.
articles.body: Dos años después, Daniel Richardson (3-0) regresa a WOW FC. El peleador del Climent Club, consolidado con un interesante 3-0 en su carrera como profesional, peleará este fin de semana en WOW 33 Vitoria contra el durísimo Willmar Quirama (4-0-1) en una prueba de nivel para saber a qué puede aspirar Richardson. En la previa de este combate, atiende a MARCA. Pregunta. Por fin llega a WOW. ¿Cómo ha vivido estos meses desde que se anunció su fichaje? Respuesta. La verdad que sé de la pelea ya 11 semanas atrás. Así que he tenido un muy buen ‘training camp’. Es algo que siempre da gusto, ¿no?, que no sea algo en corto aviso. Y muy bien, la verdad que creo que he crecido bastante estas semanas como peleador. El reto de pelear con Quirama, volver a WOW… un poquito la situación cambiante me ha hecho exigirme aún más en los entrenamientos. Así que muy bien, la verdad. P. Hay muchas expectativas por verle pelear… R. No le doy mucha importancia en el sentido de que yo también quiero verme pelear. Al final esto es mi vida, mi día a día, lo que yo hago, por todo lo que he trabajado… así que todo lo que hay externo, el ruido… no es algo que me quite el sueño la verdad. Yo hago esto por y para mí, y para mi familia y la gente que me quiere. Es verdad que agradezco la atención, agradezco la presión en ese sentido, ¿no?, pero me parece un privilegio que ocurre cuando creo que haces las cosas bien, cuando la gente espera cosas de ti… si nadie espera nada de mí sería un poco estar haciendo las cosas mal. Así que más que sentirlo como presión lo agradezco, me parece algo positivo. P. Pero para el Climent Club siempre ha habido muchos focos. ¿Se han acostumbrado ya a eso? R. Llevo compitiendo desde que tengo 12 años así que el competir no es algo tampoco que me suponga algo súper estresante y también a lo mejor mi perspectiva de cómo veo el mundo no sé… siento que todos vamos a morir en menos de 60-70 años, ¿no?. Sé que es un poco cínico, pero no le doy la importancia a lo mejor a lo que otras personas le darían. Me parece la vida como unos años que tenemos aquí en este mundo, en esta vida para aprender y no la voy a vivir perdiendo el tiempo… así que no vería como como fallar nada de lo que pasa en mi vida. Yo lo doy absolutamente todo en mi día a día, persigo mis sueños, pienso que voy a cumplirlos y si no los cumplo pues no me quedaré con la duda. Ese es mi pensamiento, entonces no me pongo presión extra con pensamientos ajenos. P. ¿Mantener el invicto supone presión? R. Eso lo decide Dios, yo soy creyente y entonces pienso que es algo ajeno. Ya no me pesa, con el tiempo como peleador estoy madurando. Antes, como amateur, quizás pensaba eso de ‘buah, no puedo perder’... pero es que a día de hoy ya lo tengo como algo muy natural. Cada vez las peleas van a ser de más nivel y creo que todo el mundo cae en este deporte tarde o temprano si se queda el tiempo suficiente peleando. P. ¿Por qué WOW ahora? R. Es el momento. Ya necesitaba retos, necesitaba sentir que estaba avanzando realmente en mi carrera. Al final es verdad que las primeras peleas no me importaba dónde pelear, quería simplemente coger un poco de experiencia en la jaula con los rounds de 5 minutos, con las guantillas de 4 onzas, con los codos… pero ya después de tres peleas creo que el colchón por así decir de experiencia está ahí. P. Quirama, que también está invicto, es una prueba muy dura para arrancar. R. A mí me gusta. Me parece una buena pelea. De hecho, cuando era el número uno del ranking WOW amateur y vi a Quirama pelear una noche… dije que quería pelear con él. Eso fue en 2024. Me parece una pelea muy similar en cuanto a los tiempos de nuestra carrera: hemos debutado en Pro más o menos a la vez, él va 4-0 ahora y yo 3-0… Me gusta la pelea, me parece entretenida y es lo que quería. P. ¿Qué tipo de combate espera? Usted es muy clínico, estratégico… y Quirama ha tenido peleas caóticas. R. A ver, yo pienso que voy a hacer lo que hago siempre con mi estilo porque yo obligo a pelear ese tipo de pelea. Creo que, bueno, con todo el respeto hacia Ionescu, yo no soy Ionescu… yo no voy a entrar a ese caos de forma descontrolada. Y creo que Quirama también aprendió de eso. Yo voy a hacer mi juego, voy a pelear como peleo siempre… He visto todas sus peleas varias veces y he visto cosas que se ve que le gustan hacer en según qué momento y demás, pero bueno, este deporte es como es. Yo tengo mi game plan, eso está claro. P. ¿El objetivo es hacer carrera dentro de WOW y llegar al cinturón? R. Sí. Realmente más allá de WOW no veo necesario ir a ningún otro lado ahora mismo. Estamos en casa, WOW tiene el Fight Pass, siempre hay un gran público en los eventos, tienes los ojos de los medios encima… no me sirve de nada irme a un Cage Warriors o irme a una promotora de este estilo ahora mismo. Creo que lo tengo todo con WOW. Agradecido con la oportunidad que me han brindado esta vez, así que mi idea es hacer mínimamente los dos años que tengo de contrato con ellos… y ya espero estar en una posición para saltar. P. WOW, si no me equivoco, está ofreciendo ahora contratos de dos años como el suyo y se compromete mínimo a ofrecer tres peleas al año. R. Sí, y me gustaría hacerlas. No descartaría del todo a lo mejor pelar en diciembre, no sé, tampoco he hablado con nadie… pero no descartaría hacer otra antes de acabar el año. Luego el año que viene mínimo otras tres sí. Quiero estar activo. P. Todo el mundo quiere pelear en Valencia o Madrid… R. Valencia me gusta pero peleando en octubre noviembre no es algo inteligente, está descartado. Pero para el año que viene, buah, me encantaría la verdad. Para mí sería cumplir un sueño pelear en el Roig Arena. Vendría mucha gente de casa y es un escenario que me parece digno de cualquier plataforma de MMA. P. Hace unos meses fichó por Iridium, una agencia de representación con numerosos luchadores en UFC. ¿Qué planes tienen para usted? R. Lo de WOW es verdad que había llegado antes de hablar con Jason pero sí que le pregunté, le envié el contrato, tuvimos conversaciones y desde su punto de vista también era la mejor opción a tomar. Al final el plan está claro: desde WOW se puede ir directamente a UFC. Lo ha hecho Fabià, lo hizo Hecher, en su día Aleksandre… está claro que ahora el título de WOW tiene un peso grande, al igual que lo ha tenido en Francia promotoras como Hexagone o Ares. P. Voy a ser directo: ¿Cree que se habla poco de usted? R. A ver, yo creo que todo el mundo que sigue este deporte a nivel nacional sabe por lo menos quién soy… o en algún momento me ha visto o tiene algún pensamiento de mí. ¿Que se hable poco de mí? Pues sinceramente creo que todo el mundo está en su lugar, y si yo para que la gente hable más de mí me lo tengo que ganar a pico y pala, pues lo haré, seguiré peleando y seguiré trabajando. Creo que en la vida no se te da nada que no te mereces. Yo creo que estoy en la posición en la que tengo que estar. Tengo una frase puesta en mi biografía que es ‘vuelvete imposible de ignorar’... pero la fama no es algo que yo quiera ni necesite, ni hago esto por fama. Es verdad que esto es algo que he cambiado en mi mentalidad en los últimos dos años. Yo no quiero fama como tal, yo quiero reconocimiento por mi trabajo. Yo no hago esto para ser famoso ni porque quiera una suma de dinero, ni nada por el estilo. Hago esto porque me gusta, lo amo y es una de las cosas que me trae felicidad y paz en mi vida. Y no necesito la aprobación del resto, sinceramente. Es algo que ha cambiado. P. Me recuerda un poco a Volkanovski cuando dijo que no peleaba por títulos o legado, sino únicamente por su familia. R. Sí, ¿y quién conocía a Volkanovski cuando tenía 25 años?. La MMA es un deporte en el que pasas de desapercibido un año a otro ser el mayor prospecto. Mira Vallejos o gente así: dos años y medio, nadie lo conoce o tal... y ahora es una estrella de UFC. Así es este deporte. P. Para acabar: ¿Cómo se ve en 2027? R. Pues me veo saliendo victorioso ahora el 24 de octubre. No sabría decirte si podría pelear en diciembre o no, pero también es algo que no descarto. Me gustaría irme a principio de año a Tailandia, hacer otro mes ahí de training camp porque crecí bastante y es una experiencia que me gustaría hacer cada año si Dios me lo permite… y como te he dicho, mantenerme activo: tres peleas al año en WOW.

articles.title: Video: SteveWillDoIt Gifts Brendan Allen A Brand New Cadillac
articles.summary: Brendan Allen had a great night at UFC Vegas 122 a couple weeks ago, and it’s still getting better. In the main event, Allen took on Christian Leroy Duncan a...
articles.body:
Brendan Allen had a great night at UFC Vegas 122 a couple weeks ago, and it's still getting better.

In the main event, Allen took on Christian Leroy Duncan and held off the Englishman's rise in a bloody five-round scrap. In the very last round of their competitive battle, Allen was able to take his opponent's back and lock in the submission (watch here) , securing an extra $100k bonus as a result of his late finish. As it turns out, that would not be Allen's only bonus stemming from the evening!

Social media star SteveWillDoIt loves to throw money around and is a supporter of "All In." After Allen's big win, SteveWillDoIt (real name Stephen Deleonardis) paid for a brand new Cadillac for the surging 185-pound contender. "Congrats to my fighter Brandan Allen," Deleonardis wrote on X . "This mother f—ker just got a caddilac as a performance bonus!!!!"

If the nearly $190k wire transfer wasn't proof enough, Allen posted a video showing off his new wheels still in the dealership and thanking SteveWillDoIt and his associated companies/sponsors.

"We're here at Cadillac New Orleans," Allen said. "There that fight bonus from your boy SteveWillDoIt … this is f—king insane. Absolutely gorgeous man."

After the big win, Allen has won four straight bouts and successfully reasserted himself into the Middleweight title mix. He's been gunning for a grudge match versus former champion Dricus du Plessis for years now , and perhaps the timing is finally right. Either way, Allen should find himself in a title eliminator bout sooner rather than later, and he has a fancy new car to get him safely to the gym.

articles.title: “Rumors and talk”: Islam Makhachev’s manager gives final say on rumored bout with Carlos Prates at UFC 336
articles.summary: A rumored fight between Islam Makhachev and Carlos Prates at UFC 336 in Toronto is currently far from being finalized.
articles.body: A rumored fight between Islam Makhachev and Carlos Prates at UFC 336 in Toronto is currently far from being finalized. Makhachev’s manager has played down the growing reports surrounding a possible January showdown, saying negotiations are still ongoing and nothing has been confirmed.The welterweight champion has been linked with Prates following his recent run in the UFC. However, Makhachev’s team has made it clear that fans should not treat the rumored matchup as official. The event, opponent and date are yet to be finalized, despite increasing speculation about a potential UFC 336 fight.Islam Makhachev vs Carlos Prates remains only a rumorIslam Makhachev’s manager Ali Abdelaziz addressed the speculation in comments to Russian outlet Ushatayka. He confirmed that discussions are taking place but stressed that the potential fight is nowhere near becoming official.“As of now, it’s not close to becoming a reality. It’s all just rumors and talk. Negotiations are ongoing, but confirming he’ll fight on a certain date and against a certain opponent is still far from realistic”, he said.The comments come after reports linked Makhachev with a January return at UFC 336 in Toronto. Carlos Prates has emerged as one of the names being discussed as a possible opponent.Prates has attracted significant attention during his UFC career because of his dangerous striking and rapid rise through the welterweight division. A fight against Makhachev would represent one of the biggest opportunities of his career.However, there is currently no official confirmation from the UFC that Makhachev will compete at UFC 336. There is also no confirmed agreement between the champion and Prates.Makhachev remains one of the biggest names in the UFC. The Russian fighter moved to welterweight after an outstanding run at lightweight. He previously held the UFC lightweight championship before making the move up and winning a second UFC title.His professional record stands at 29-1. He has also built an impressive winning streak inside the UFC and remains at the top of the promotion’s pound-for-pound rankings.Makhachev most recently defended his welterweight title against Ian Machado Garry at UFC 330 in Philadelphia. He earned a unanimous decision after a dominant performance in the grappling exchanges.Machado Garry had moments of success with his striking, but Makhachev’s pressure and wrestling remained decisive. The victory extended Makhachev’s UFC winning streak to 17 fights.Away from fighting, Makhachev has also taken on a new challenge. He recently enrolled as a master’s student at Plekhanov Russian University of Economics’ Dubai branch.The university praised the champion for continuing his education while competing at the highest level of MMA.For now, Makhachev’s next opponent remains uncertain. articles.title: Merab Dvalishvili looks shredded after revealing brutal 12kg weight cut ahead of Petr Yan trilogy fight at UFC 333
articles.summary: Merab Dvalishvili is looking extremely lean just days before his highly anticipated rematch with Petr Yan.
articles.body: Merab Dvalishvili is looking extremely lean just days before his highly anticipated rematch with Petr Yan. The former UFC bantamweight champion has already lost 7 kilograms (15 pounds) and says he still has another 5 kilograms (11 pounds) to cut before stepping on the scales.The Georgian fighter admitted that the final part of the weight cut will be difficult. His comments have highlighted just how demanding the final days can be for a fighter competing at 135 pounds. Dvalishvili and Yan will meet again this Saturday at UFC 333, with the bantamweight title at stake.Merab Dvalishvili faces tough final 5kg before Petr Yan fightMerab Dvalishvili has revealed that he has already dropped a significant amount of weight ahead of his showdown with Petr Yan. However, the former champion still needs to lose another 5 kilograms before reaching the bantamweight limit.“I cut 7 kgs [15 lbs] already and 5 kgs [11 lbs] left. This 5 kg will be tough, as you see I’m already skinny”, he said.The statement came alongside footage showing Dvalishvili looking noticeably shredded during fight week. His lean appearance has attracted plenty of attention from MMA fans.In total, Dvalishvili is targeting a 12-kilogram (26.4-pound) reduction. Losing that much weight is a major physical challenge for any fighter. The final stage can become especially difficult when an athlete is already carrying very little body fat.Dvalishvili is preparing for one of the biggest fights of his career. He will face Yan for the third time in a rivalry that has already produced two closely watched championship-level contests.Their first meeting took place in March 2023. Dvalishvili defeated Yan by unanimous decision after producing one of the most relentless performances of his career. He constantly pressured the Russian and attempted 49 takedowns, completing 11 of them.Yan later got his revenge in their second meeting at UFC 323 in December 2025. He defeated Dvalishvili by unanimous decision and reclaimed the bantamweight championship.Yan’s performance was built around strong takedown defense and accurate striking. He stopped 27 of Dvalishvili’s 29 takedown attempts while finding success with his own offense.The result left the rivalry tied at 1-1. Their upcoming fight will therefore decide who gets the upper hand in the trilogy.Yan enters the contest as the reigning UFC bantamweight champion. He will be looking to defend his title and defeat Dvalishvili for a second consecutive time.Dvalishvili, meanwhile, will be determined to reclaim the championship. His trademark style depends heavily on pressure, movement and repeated wrestling attacks.That makes his weight cut particularly important. His ability to maintain energy and cardio could play a major role in the five-round contest.UFC 333 will take place on Saturday, October 24, at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. articles.title: MVP: MMA fighters should 'form a union' over pay, says Michael 'Venom' Page
articles.summary: Michael 'Venom' Page says MMA fighters need to form a union and "move as one" if they want to secure better pay in the sport.
articles.body:
Michael 'Venom' Page says MMA fighters need to form a union and "move as one" if they want to secure better pay in the sport.

The 39-year-old signed a deal with Misfits Boxing earlier this month after leaving the UFC.

Page, better known as MVP, won five of his six bouts in the UFC after debuting in 2024 but was critical of the money its fighters earn , compared with top-level athletes in other sports.

After joining Misfits, where Page says he will earn "a lot more" than he did in the UFC, the Briton wants to use his platform to empower fellow fighters.

Page points to the Muhammad Ali Act - a 2000 US law designed to protect boxers' rights and combat potential monopolies - as something which he'd like to replicate in MMA.

"It's less about speaking out now, it's more about forming a union and coming together. We have to move as one," Page told BBC Sport.

"If all fighters said 'we're not gonna do it', then UFC doesn't exist. That's the important thing for fighters to remember. It's not just the machine of UFC, you guys are the nuts and bolts that help the machine move.

"A fighters union is what's important - the Muhammad Ali Act is what has allowed boxers to be paid well and the same thing needs to happen in MMA."

Fighter pay has been questioned by athletes and the media this year after boxer Conor Benn signed a reported £11m one-fight deal with Zuffa Boxing.

Zuffa Boxing is owned by UFC president Dana White, so critics have asked why the 57-year-old isn't paying similar amounts to his MMA fighters under contract.

White has repeatedly defended fighter pay in the UFC, referencing the promotion's £5.7bn broadcast deal with Paramount.

Last week, after criticism from UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland , White pointed to the American signing a new contract in May.

Page says criticism like that of Strickland is "common" in the UFC, but most fighters don't speak out in case of repercussions.

"You speak to other athletes and it's a very common thing. Most people are not willing to say anything because it will affect them," said Page.

"I feel if I don't say anything, silence is going along with it and you're part of the problem. But I also understand you have your own bills to pay, so I'm not against anyone that doesn't either.

"If more people spoke out then they'd have to do something but it's difficult if we're not doing it as a unit, you can get ousted and other things can happen."

Page says he is "excited" to box in Misfits, and discussions have taken place about incorporating MMA into the promotion, but his main goal is to create a healthier financial space for the younger generation.

"The aim is to get them well paid, well looked after and well treated in the MMA space and bring competition against other shows," said Page.

"Which is good for fighters, it means they have alternative spaces to go to and they can negotiate better because of it.

"I see people in the UFC still struggling and I don't think there's another sport you can get to the top of your field and be struggling financially. I definitely want better for fighters."

Despite his criticisms of fighter pay, Page says he "for the most part loved" his time in the UFC.

He praised the promotion's staff, its Performance Institute - regarded as the gold standard among MMA training facilities - and its fans.

However, Page, who won all of his fights in the promotion by decision, faced criticism from fans over his lack of knockouts and admits he might have approached things differently in hindsight.

"I wish I could have done more with my performances, but overall I loved it," he said.

"I think the game has slightly shifted. It's not about who's the most skilled anymore, it's about guys who are willing to put themselves through hell and shave years off their life every single time they fight.

"If I was a bit more aware of that I would have shifted a little bit to try and compensate for that."

Page says he's aiming to make his debut in Misfits "in the first part of next year" but it has not been decided if it will be under boxing or MMA rules.

He mentioned former UFC stars Nate Diaz and Darren Till as interesting match-ups, but reiterated that no discussions about potential opponents have taken place yet.

articles.title: Fabio Wardley offered route back to world title after 'rest and recovery' - 'We'll see where we go. He's a dangerous man'
articles.summary: Promoter Frank Warren believes Fabio Wardley can return to world title contention if the former WBO heavyweight champion chooses to continue boxing; Wardley lost a second consecutive bout to Daniel Dubois on Saturday when the Londoner beat him in two rounds at the O2 Arena
articles.body:
Wardley was unable to regain the WBO world title after he was stopped in the second round of his second fight with Dubois at The O2 on Saturday.

But his manager Mike Ofo firmly believes that Wardley can challenge one of the other world champions after a "well-earned rest".

Ofo told Sky Sports : "Fabio has had a remarkable run, and there is no doubt that he still has a bright future ahead of him.

"Now is the time for him to enjoy a well-earned rest, to recover and consider his options. His journey has already been nothing short of remarkable, an extraordinary story of grit, determination and achievement.

"Clearly, he has never shied away from a challenge and has chosen to face the toughest opponents at every turn.

"I fully expect him to continue competing at the very highest levels of the sport and to win another world title if that is what he chooses to do."

Oleksandr Usyk's decision to vacate his world titles has opened up new opportunities as Murat Gassiev holds a WBA title, while Agit Kabayel is the WBC champion, and Filip Hrgovic holds the IBF belt.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will also fight for the WBA 'super' title in Cardiff on December 11.

Promoter Frank Warren intends to steer Wardley back into world title contention.

Asked if Wardley remains a threat to the division's top fighters, Warren told Sky Sports ' Toe 2 Toe podcast: "He's knocked over guys that have never been knocked over before.

"If he catches you, you're in trouble, and he's capable of doing that, but he's got to take a rest now and he's got to weigh up his chances and where he thinks he can go.

"I'm sure when he does come back, he'll have, as we call it in the trade, a warm-up fight. But if he does come back, he'll want to fight for a title again. He's a former world champion."

Wardley has reached the elite level of the sport, despite turning professional after a spell as a 'white-collar fighter' and Warren believes his remarkable success story can have another chapter.

"He'll be out for a while now and let him just rest and come back; if he does come back, and we'll see where we go with him," Warren said.

"You've got to look at some of the wins he's had. He beat Joe Parker, who was ranked No 1 in the world and everyone was saying, 'When is he going to get his shot at a world title?'

"They were backing Joe Parker to beat Daniel and to give Usyk a real tough fight and he beat him, he stopped him. I take my hat off to him.

"All of the things you've just mentioned, he never had a single amateur fight, learnt on the job, and look where he got himself, so he should be unbelievably proud of himself.

"He's a big puncher. You look at that knockout he had with Frazer Clarke. The first fight was a good fight but the second one he knocked him out in the first round and look what he did to Justis Huni. Massively behind against a very good boxer and he knocked him over. Even with Daniel, he had him on the floor twice in their first fight. He's a dangerous man.

"You look back over the years and I'm not saying he's Lennox Lewis, but Lennox, he lost against Hasim Rahman, he lost against Oliver McCall but down the road he avenged those defeats.

"A lot of these guys have been beaten in fights over the years and this era now, there's some really good fighters out there."

articles.title: Rise and shine! West Coast fans are gonna hate the UFC 333 special start time
articles.summary: Wakey! Wakey! Eggs and bakey!
articles.body:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is traveling to "Fight Island" in Abu Dhabi for the upcoming UFC 333 mixed martial arts (MMA) event on Paramount+ from inside Etihad Arena. The good news is that most stateside fans will be wrapped by mid-to-late afternoon and will have Saturday night to do … whatever it is people do on a Saturday night. Is dressing in neon colors and hanging out at the local roller rink still a thing?

Additional main card matchups include the flyweight fracas pitting Lone'er Kavanagh against Ramazan Temirov, while Alexander Volkov and Rizvan Kuniev hook 'em up at 265 pounds. In addition, Aaron Pico collides with Losene Keita in featherweight action.

articles.title: Dana White & UFC producing Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury claims once again dismissed
articles.summary: After months of waiting around and seeing rumors emerge, Netflix has now confirmed the much-awaited Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury fight for later this year....
articles.body:
After months of waiting around and seeing rumors emerge, Netflix has now confirmed the much-awaited Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury fight for later this year. The fight is now set to take place on Dec. 11, 2026, at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

A few weeks ago, UFC president Dana White claimed to have a significant role in promoting and producing the Fury vs. Joshua fight. However, Matchroom Boxing's Eddie Hearn publicly disagreed with White's alleged involvement. This soon followed a back-and-forth banter between the two , with the Misfits Boxing co-founder also suggesting a match between the two.

While White insists on his involvement in the fight , Hearn continues to claim that the UFC President is contractually barred from having any involvement in the Joshua vs. Fury boxing match.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Eddie Hearn has been Joshua's promoter since he made his professional debut in 2013. Joshua's contract for his fight with Fury is believed to specifically state that Dana White cannot be involved in the event.

"Under our contract, he can't. So that's really where we stand on it. Sela has confirmed to us in writing that Dana White and the UFC are not doing the production for this show. So, we have to go through the same process, blah blah blah.

"We will speak to Netflix and guess what? Whisper, the production company that did the production for Fury/Makhmudov, they have a contract to do the production for Fury vs. AJ on Netflix," Hearn said while speaking on iFL TV on YouTube.

Hearn finished by claiming that if White and the UFC want to speak with him regarding changing the contract about the production, he is open to a conversation. Despite the disagreements, the fight is still on for Dec. 2026.

articles.title: Former UFC champion explains why he's up for 'Proper' challenge
articles.summary: "The fight definitely makes sense." But does it?
articles.body:
Former UFC champion Belal Muhammad wants a "Proper" challenge.

Muhammad (24-6 MMA, 15-6 UFC) has been on a recent losing streak and sees a matchup against Mike Malott as a real possibility that could benefit both fighters. Malott (15-2-1 MMA, 8-1 UFC) is coming off a Knockout of the Year-contending finish of Joaquin Buckley in the main event of UFC Fight Night 291 on his home country's soil. Malott doesn't call out opponents directly, but others have done it for him.

"People are bringing up my name a lot, for sure," Muhammad said in a YouTube video. "The fight definitely makes sense."

Muhammad last fought at UFC Fight Night 278, where he lost a unanimous decision to Gabriel Bonfim in the main event. That result marked his third consecutive loss in a rough stretch that includes losses to former champ Jack Della Maddalena and former title challenger Ian Machado Garry . Muhammad has been wanting to face fellow former champion Kamaru Usman for some time now, but he isn't willing to sit out much longer.

"Obviously, when I'm looking at the division, I'm looking at who I want to fight," Muhammad said. "You know we want to fight Usman, but I'm not going to sit there and wait."

For Malott, a fight against Muhammad would make sense. Malott is on a five-fight winning streak, and despite Muhammad's skid, the fight represents a step up in competition. Malott has never faced a former UFC titleholder in the octagon. The closest on his resume is former title challenger Gilbert Burns.

Muhammad wants to get back to action soon, and January's UFC 336 in Toronto could be a good fit for Malott to fight again in Canada. In the latest USA TODAY Sports/MMA Junkie welterweight rankings , Muhammad holds the No. 7 spot, while Malott ranks No. 9.

"When I'm looking at who's hot right now, who's on a streak, Mike Malott got a good winning streak going," Muhammad said. "A win over him puts you in a good spot, puts you back into the mix, and reminds people who you are. So, for myself, it's one of those situations where if Usman's not trying to go, for sure, 'Proper' Mike Malott would definitely be a yes on my end. So, we'll see what the UFC does. We'll see what the UFC brings and what they want to do with it."
